note: The manager owns this file. It is structured ON PURPOSE — the previous loop kept its state as a prose header, which degenerated into a 4,000-character run-on paragraph of abbreviations that no longer carried signal. Structure resists that.

menu.note: The menu is DATA, not prose in a skill file, so the manager can extend it (ladder rung 3). Adding a domain or a kind here is a legitimate strategic move.

kinds.name: New element
kinds.what: a thing the town did not contain

kinds.name: New CA rule
kinds.what: a new per-cell rule that makes the grid evolve

kinds.name: Deepen
kinds.what: make an existing system richer, or wire two together

kinds.name: Connect
kinds.what: link two places or systems that ignore each other

kinds.name: Polish
kinds.what: make what is there read better; add nothing

kinds.name: Interaction/UX
kinds.what: how you read, poke or navigate the diorama

kinds.name: Scale/World
kinds.what: change the size, span or time of the world itself

kinds.name: Harness
kinds.what: the loop's own instruments — gates, probes, runlog, stats. Changes nothing a viewer sees, and does NOT count toward a domain's balance

coverage.note: domain -> kind -> iteration numbers. Pre-loop work (CHANGELOG iterations 1-31, hand-driven) is recorded as `pre` so the manager knows the ground it stands on.

skyxpolish.why: 6 polish entries, more than any other cell, on the best-drawn system in the town. The lowest-yield move available. Sky work from here is Deepen or Connect.

inventory.note: What the town ALREADY CONTAINS, in the words a brief would use. NOUNS plus the symbol names and probe files a brief must name — one line per system, 300 bytes each, ENFORCED by rotate-ledger.mjs. Measurements and histories belong in the ledger. Read this before you build: it is the antidote to the previous loop’s terminal failure, nine iterations that each surveyed the world, found everything already existed, and exited.
courtyard: walled garden, organic bed ring, four arch entrances (2 TUNNEL, 2 SLOT), benches, desire paths from foot wear, daisies, ivy on the gatehouse, a pre-dawn sweeper, one linden (drawTree, CX/CY)
planting CA — 11 species, bloom stages, seeding from mature neighbours, crowding, age dieback; rain accelerates every growth term

the beds read the YEAR — growF()/dieF()/bloomCap() off warmth, lawn health in groundCol; bloomCap is a CEILING and per-cell hardiness holds ~1/7 of cells at it, so winter is blooms scattered in turned earth. probes/beds-year.mjs
lane: kiosk, pavement cafe with claimable tables, awnings, washing lines, planters, street lamps, benches
market day every 4th day, three stalls; marketRaise(i) stages each stall up and down as clamps on one 0..1 progress
washing comes in before the rain — per-garment thresholds on weatherComing(), plus a dusk ramp; never all in one frame

the working day hangs off the SUN — kioskOpen/marketOpen/marketClose/marketRaise/sweeper/wind announcement are offsets from sunUp/sunDown; MK_MIN_SPAN floors winter, MK_EARLIEST holds the summer raise. probes/working-day.mjs

the stalls sell what the plots grew — produce[] written only by harvestPlot(); stockMarket() latches it once per market day into mkShelf; marketRaise(i) gates on mkTrades(i) (MK_NEED) so a thin year raises fewer stalls. Pitches are real vegetables, MK_CAP carries over. probes/market-year.mjs

the town's ONE evening place — a lit door in the gatehouse front (TAP_DOOR, drawTapDoor). tapOpen() opens on sunDown-3 floored at TAP_EARLIEST and shuts by the CLOCK at 03.00, so WINTER's evening is the longest; tapF() is the 0..1 every draw mixes on. probes/evening-door.mjs
street: cross street with two footways, roadway, curbs, street lamps, four street trees in stone pits (TREE_PITS, drawLaneTree)
allotment block of 17 plots, timber fence, gates, shed, an alley cut through the block
harvest cycle — harvestPlot() lifts a mature 3x2 bed whole, bAge doubles as a fallow clock, then re-sown as a row under plotCrop(). census planting.harvested
spawnAllotAgent() — the allotments' own arrival source, rate on ripePlots(); gardeners walk out carrying a basket (a.crop)

seasonal canopy on all 13 trees — leafOut/leafFresh/leafDeep/leafTurn/leafShed + leafCol(base,k) off seasonPhase, bare in winter behind drawBoughs(); leafFallF() drives falling leaves. probes/canopy-year.mjs, year-strip.mjs
orchard year on the fruit:1 flag — blossomF() (white crown, out ahead of the leaves) and fruitF() (green->red, gone before the tree is bare)
winter hardiness grain-matched to the PLOT — SPECIES.hardy:1 (cabbages), plotStands(x,y) off plotCrop(); which plots stand rotates with the harvest. probes/allot-year.mjs, allot-shots.mjs
plaza: plaza with a fountain and a paved roundel (PATH), four tree pits, benches; quay with benches along the river

spawnEastAgent() — the east quarter's own arrival source (eastCap/eastRate, a.east, excluded from laneCount, eastOpen() on daylight); enters by the alley, quay head or park gate, visits one stop, leaves the way it came. census life.inEast

PAVING + pavingAt(x,y) — the ONE predicate naming which paving a cell is (lane, bridge, cross street, mouth, plaza, quay, towpath, court). Each carries its crumbs line AND the box its birds land in; crumbSpot() staggers three birds clear of the basin. probes/paving-places.mjs
river: river, one rowboat, three-arch bridge, towpath, church with tower and nave, bandstand, four orchard trees, jetty, park gate
pigeons that flush off the belfry when the bell rings, from a finite roost that refills

byTheWater() — the ONE predicate for the three places a person can see the river (quay and rail, bridge deck, towpath); boatWatch() is its only reader, a future river event should read it rather than re-derive it
boatWatch() — one glance per passing boat (a.watch, ticked at the top of stepAgent so it never holds anybody)
a parapet stop mid-span (PARAPET_Y, PARAPET_Z), served mainly from spawnEastAgent

the water reads the YEAR — riverRun() drives drawRiverFlow(t): drift speed, streak count and length, channel colour (riverCol -> RIVER_COLD/RIVER_GREEN), width of the deep mid-channel. probes/river-year.mjs, river-shots.mjs

the rowboat is a fair-weather thing — boatRate() thins as the water rises (BOAT_SWING, BOAT_FLOOR binding through winter), boatSpeed() takes BOAT_DRIFT of the current. ONE boat, so its year reads as PRESENCE not boats/day

the BANDSTAND has a summer concert — bandF() stages three BAND_PLAYERS (cues 0.10/0.30/0.50) and bunting up and back down on ONE 0..1; isBandDay() is hash(day,617) vs bandChance() off warmth, so July plays and February does not. probes/bandstand-year.mjs, bandstand-shots.mjs
sky: day/night cycle (55 s day), sun and moon arc, backdrop hills, chimney smoke, a balloon; night window lighting is drawWindow()’s lit + the LIT[] glow pass, one hash per building per day, every window switching together at nightF > 0.3
isWindy() — wind days, read by the ticker, leaf fall, smoke drift, tree sway, washing-line swing, the morning wind announcement
cloudCover() — one slow rate-capped scalar; fronts build over ~half a day and break after rain; sun and moon veiled, stars put out, drifting banks
weatherComing() — the ramped rain-is-coming predicate off cloudCover(), damped by daylight because people anticipate by looking up; three readers at their own trigger points
rainFall — a 0..1 shower intensity beside the raining boolean; drops, overcast tint, pond rings, water sparkle and chimney smoke all read it

season() — the YEAR. Cyclic over SEASON_LEN 26 days (~24 real min), phase 0 = midwinter, anchored at SEASON_START 0.25 where every seasoned term equals the constant it replaced. NINE READERS: day length, light, beds, trees, the working day, pop caps, weather, river, allotments. census clock.season

the weather reads the year — greyF() drives front frequency, depth and spellLen() while showerRate/showerLen/showerHard move the OPPOSITE way, so summer’s rare showers are the hard ones and the annual total holds. Rain can start in the dark. probes/weather-year.mjs

the ground reads the lid — shadowF() with shSpread() and shOffset(), so a cast shadow fades, widens and retracts together; eight sites, a real blur on the cached ground layer behind CAN_BLUR. probes/shadow-cover.mjs, ground-relight.mjs
life: walkers with itineraries, courtyard and street; eastern itineraries — plaza bench, fountain gaze, quay rail, quay bench, towpath, church green, allotment plot, bridge parapet
cafe sitters who claim and release a table; market and kiosk browsers; ducks, swans, butterflies, fireflies, birds, one night cat, falling leaves
a clock that strikes and a church bell that answers it at nine and eighteen from day 2; walkers break stride and look up while it rings (a.listen)
greetPass — two passing within 0.9-1.6 cells may stop, turn and talk (a.greet, chatCool)

EVERY sitter reads the sky — SIT_REFUSE turns a seat down, skyLifts(a) gives one up off a per-agent a.wary, umbrellas on their own band. The gate is what you are DOING, not a.street. A refused courtyard seat takes routeToExit(); a picnic pair judges once for both (a.mate). probes/seats-out.mjs
__entities() carries role, act, watch and raindrops per person, with a stable id — the seam a behaviour probe reads instead of a bespoke hook

yearBusy(ex) multiplies the DAYLIGHT term of capacity/laneCap/eastCap only, never their fixed share (EX_COURT/EX_LANE/EX_EAST; eastCap keeps Math.min(7,...)). POP_FLOOR + scarcity lift the three arrival RATES only. probes/season-year.mjs

the audience is the town's one STANDING crowd — spawnConcertAgent(), its own source and BAND_TICK, out of neither eastCount nor laneCount; nine claimed BAND_SLOTS hold them 1.99 cells apart for as long as they stand, and a.leaveAt thins them across the strike

spawnTapAgent() — the evening door's own arrivals, out of the courtyard south arch (a.tap, four TAP_SLOTS, off laneCount, no scarcity); tapServing() stops sending TAP_LAST hours before the shut so the pavement empties on its own timers. a.cup draws standing
sill: the SILL under the canvas — #plate, #daytime (day + hour), #season, #ticker, #stats, #ctrl (Pause, 1x/3x/8x). Ticker and stats hidden under 640px except during an invitation. A ResizeObserver on the frame, because the sill BORROWS space and that resizes the picture with no resize event
the ticker is an ordered queue, not an overwrite — TICK_DWELL 2.5 real s, cap 2, staleness cut; a follow-on enqueues only when its antecedent is DISPLAYED (lineDwell)
the sill NAMES the year — seasonLabel() on seasonPhase, eight names, sectors CENTRED on their phase; #season drops into the caption slot below 640px. probes/sill-year.mjs

the season is a BUTTON and reads as one — stepSkip()/simSub()/skipEase() run the town on a quarter as a sub-stepped fast-forward landing on a whole sim day, four clicks to the year; #season underlined, 30px/29px hit box at zero layout cost. probes/season-skip.mjs, season-invite.mjs

the NAMING — what is under the pointer is named in the sill (borrows the ticker box; a TAP names on a phone). bSp/bSt vs bedCap(x,y), plots off plotCrop, places off pavingAt/WATERS, 13 trees hit-tested in SCREEN space vs crowns[]. NAME_SETTLE. probes/naming.mjs

THE DIORAMA IS CLICKABLE and says so once — answersTouch(x,y) is the ONE predicate (~64% of the frame), read by both cursor and handler: seeds, a daisy, crumbs, a coin, a pebble. Invitations are a QUEUE, OFFERS[] of two, each spent when it comes up. probes/touch-hint.mjs

openCues.note: FRONT_DEEP lets deep-winter cover CLAMP at a saturated 1.000 for whole spells, so no drawn term has range left above ~0.95: a future how-heavy-is-this-lid signal cannot be read off cover alone.
the picnic pair shares one sky decision but keeps two independent sit timers (each half draws its own on arrival), so the sky can no longer split a pair but an ordinary afternoon still can. a.mate.
the offer queue bounds SPACING but not ARRIVAL: offerInvite waits for tickerFree(), so a first offer on a busy day inherits an arrival time nothing floors (17.4 s vs 30.1 s measured).

BAND_DUSK is a hand-computed clearance between the strike ramp and eastOpen(). Nothing ASSERTS it: move BAND_DOWN, BAND_LEN or leaveAt and the green goes back to emptying in one frame, which only an arrival series can see.
motion.mjs sums a shower’s rises and falls into one jumps figure, but only a FALL is the bug it exists for. Splitting them would make the night cell attributable instead of advisory.

birds hop a +/-0.4 random walk with no separation term (a pair measured 0.2 cells apart). #32 answered the STANDING case with claimed slots; a bird that keeps moving wants a separation term or a claimed perch.

the pointer names ground, plants and trees but not the LIVING things: walkers, ducks, swans, the sweeper, the boat all answer with the paving under their feet. __entities() has stable ids and crowns[] is the pattern. Was brief b34.

agents.length feeds scarcity(), and a.tap agents are now inside it, so a full pavement at the door quietly damps the three night arrival RATES that POP_FLOOR exists to lift. Small at four slots; a larger evening would want the term to read a population it is not part of.

watch.note: The east half is fed by ONE spawnLaneAgent roll under one laneCap (peaks at 9). Anything out there competes for that budget — check whether your feature needs its own arrival source before concluding it is unused. Bands: market 0.24, kiosk 0.18, cafe 0.26, allotment 0.48, plaza 0.48, quay 0.53, green 0.58. spawnEastAgent adds eastCap (max 7); its arrivals RETRACE their route, so a wider cap means single file.

THE TOWN HAS NO EVENING. Every one of the ten itinerary branches in spawnLaneAgent is gated on `sun = daylight > 0.3`, so after dark every walker falls through to the pass-through leg with no stop at all; kioskOpen, marketOpen, the band and eastOpen close too. Night is ~40% of the clock and is currently ambience (lit windows, fireflies, one cat) over a transit corridor. b35 spends this.

NOTHING EAST OF THE BRIDGE READS THE YEAR. Nine systems read season() and every one is in the courtyard, the street, the lane, the sky or the water — the position the market was in before #29. b32 spends part of it.

The observer tools are all advertised now: naming, the season label, the season button, and OFFERS[] which spent its second offer at #31. A NEW one joins that queue; it does not get a hint of its own.
